scope: Design, symbolism, physical composition, lighting behavior and future full-scale architectural interpretation of the printed Janus Arch plus removable gyroscopic/fidget oculus.

interpretation_boundary.meaning: The word 'portal' is used as the canonical architectural and symbolic interpretation of the physical assembly, not as a claim that the object opens a literal spacetime gateway.

origin_observation.event: A previously designed Janus gyroscopic/fidget assembly was placed into the circular roof opening of the previously designed and printed Janus Arch.
origin_observation.result: The independently designed parts formed a visually coherent removable top mechanism. The arch openings, roof oculus, cyan illumination and crossroads interpretation read together as a single portal architecture.

oculus_flywheel.mechanical_note: The current fit is physically observed but has not yet been dimensionally gauged as a formal interface standard.

illumination.source_context: PC internal lighting shining through and below the printed arch
illumination.architectural_effect: The cavities and passages behave visually as a luminous interior volume; cyan light spills through arches and the roof opening and reflects from the supporting surface.

crossroads.semantic: Multiple paths converge at the Janus threshold.

arch.semantic: The architectural body marks the transition between outside and inside, before and after, arrival and return.

oculus_flywheel.semantic: The rotating nested-ring form supplies the assembly with an apparent axis, state and mechanical intention.

blue_light.semantic: Illumination transforms empty cavities into a coherent interior field and makes the whole arch read as active rather than inert.

janus_semantic_mapping.beginnings_and_returns: represented by bidirectional passage through the same threshold
janus_semantic_mapping.two_faced_temporality: represented by forward/backward reading of passage and return
janus_semantic_mapping.openness: represented by keeping the passage physically open rather than sealing the arch

full_scale_architectural_interpretation.setting: A real-size Janus monument at a crossroads or plaza, derived from the printed artifact and the historical arch reference.
material_language: mechanical nested-ring oculus on the roof
lighting_language: hidden cyan-blue emitters inside wall cavities
light escaping through niches and apertures
full_scale_architectural_interpretation.night_behavior: At night the stone mass should remain visually legible while the internal cavities glow blue, making the interior threshold appear deeper than the exterior shell.
full_scale_architectural_interpretation.day_behavior: In daylight the structure reads primarily as restored classical architecture with the flywheel/oculus visible as a deliberate modern intervention.

design_principles: Keep the central passage physically open.
Do not permanently glue the oculus/flywheel into the arch; preserve removability.
Treat the circular roof opening as a modular interface in future revisions.
Preserve strong contrast between pale stone body and cyan interior light.
The flywheel must remain mechanically and visually subordinate to the arch: it activates the threshold rather than replacing it.
Lighting should originate from cavities and hidden surfaces, not from exposed decorative LED strips.
The full object should read coherently from exterior, roof and interior viewpoints.

canonical_phrases.optional_project_motto: PORTA MUTA, MUNDUS MANET. SEMPER LIBER, SEMPER PATET.

future_gates.goal: Measure opening and flywheel dimensions and define a repeatable removable fit.
If ever translated to real architecture, separate decorative 3D-print geometry from structural engineering and obtain professional structural, electrical, accessibility and public-safety design.
Define hidden lighting zones, diffusion, service access, thermal management and night/day appearance.

canonical_summary: Two independently created Janus artifacts — the restored Arch and the gyroscopic/fidget ring assembly — physically converge into one coherent composition. When interpreted at a crossroads and illuminated from within by cyan-blue light, the Arch becomes the threshold body, the roof flywheel becomes its axis/oculus, and the illuminated cavities become the active interior field. This configuration is canonically named JANUS GATE — CROSSROADS OCULUS PORTAL.
